provenance: Assistant-authored development expectations frozen before changing the method; includes M005 failures and deliberately difficult context/negation examples. Useful cases are not exhaustive relevance grades; no independent validation.

queries.text: Milk, flour and electricity are more expensive.
queries.reason: M004 miss: related dairy, grain and energy inputs.

queries.text: Chocolate ingredient inflation is squeezing profit.
queries.reason: M004 miss: cocoa is a chocolate input; ingredient alone is weak evidence.

queries.text: Bottled-water freight and fuel costs are rising.
queries.reason: M004 miss: transport and oil-related costs; product/industry still requires reader judgement.

queries.text: Grains, dairy and energy costs are increasing.

Packaging and logistics costs are increasing, putting pressure on margin.

Wheat and power bills are increasing.
queries.reason: Additional input vocabulary; power can also have non-energy meanings.

queries.text: Milk powder and grain prices rose.
queries.reason: Related pressure; exact commodity breakdown remains unknown.

queries.text: Cacao beans have become more expensive.

queries.text: Arabica coffee bean costs are rising.

queries.text: Steel smelting costs are rising.
queries.reason: No steel-specific case.

queries.text: Ingredient inflation and higher costs.
queries.reason: Ingredient is a broad input label, not a specific pressure.

queries.text: Lighter bottles and successful savings.

queries.text: No chocolate input-cost inflation is established.
queries.reason: Negation must apply before related-term matching.

queries.text: Milk cost pressure is unknown.
queries.reason: Explicit unknown is not positive cost-pressure evidence.

queries.text: No milk cost inflation; packaging costs are rising.
queries.reason: Only the positive clause should supply pressure matches.

queries.text: Not milk but packaging is more expensive.
queries.reason: Known hard wording: clause-level negation can discard a positive alternative.

queries.text: Milk costs are falling and profits are recovering.
queries.reason: Misleading: falling input costs differ from the rising-cost cases.

queries.text: Milk sales are booming.
queries.reason: Misleading: product sales growth does not establish input-cost pressure.

queries.text: Freight and fuel costs at an airline.
queries.reason: Misleading: an airline is outside the FMCG collection.

queries.text: Oil paintings are expensive for a museum.
queries.reason: Misleading: oil used in art does not establish petroleum input pressure.

queries.text: Not milk but packaging is more expensive.
Without milk cost pressure, while packaging prices rise.
No milk cost pressure and higher packaging costs.
Milk costs fall and cocoa prices rise.
Milk costs are unknown, but packaging costs are higher.
Milk costs are rising while milk sales are falling.
Milk sales are growing and packaging costs are rising.
Packaging costs rise and profits fall.

queries.text: Milk costs changed.
queries.reason: No usable cost direction in an explicit change claim.

queries.text: Milk costs may rise or fall.

queries.text: Milk costs are rising and milk costs are falling.
queries.reason: Contradictory directions for one input.

queries.text: Milk costs are no longer rising.

queries.text: Milk costs did not fall.
